headline: Refuse a MIME entity that two conforming readers would read differently, and hold one entity to a bounded number of parts, header lines and parameters.
summary: A signed S/MIME message is a MIME entity, and which octets its signature covers is decided by what its Content-Type says. RFC 2045 sec. 5.1 gives a parameter one occurrence and RFC 5322 sec. 3.6 gives a singleton field one, so an entity that names either twice has no single reading: taking the first occurrence and taking the last are both conforming, and they disagree about what the entity is. `pki.smime.verify` now refuses such an entity instead of resolving it by position. The record a verdict is read from is also copied into a store of its own, so a caller writing into its own buffer after the verdict cannot change what it reads back as verified. One entity is held to 1024 body parts, 1024 header lines and 256 Content-Type parameters, each a new `pki.constants.LIMITS` row, and the count is charged as the entity is scanned rather than after it has been taken apart.

Changed: `pki.smime.verify` and `pki.smime.decrypt` refuse an entity whose `Content-Type` declares one parameter twice, or whose header area declares one field twice. Both readings of such an entity are conforming and they differ, so the signature's own coverage is in question: `boundary` sets where the parts begin, `protocol` and `smime-type` decide whether the entity is accepted, and `micalg` decides which digest is reported back. Previously the verdict followed the order the two occurrences appeared in. `boundary="DECOY"; boundary=<real>` returned `valid: true` while the same two values swapped was refused, and a second `Content-Type: text/plain` placed after the real field returned `valid: true` while the same field placed before it was refused, which left a reader taking the last field seeing `text/plain`, finding no signature part, and reading the message as unsigned. Both orders of both shapes now raise `smime/bad-mime`. An entity naming each parameter and each field once is unaffected, and every occurrence of a field that may legally repeat, such as `Received`, is still readable from `headers`: only resolving a repeated name to a single value is refused.

One MIME entity is bounded at 1024 body parts (`pki.constants.LIMITS.MIME_MAX_PARTS`), 1024 header lines (`MIME_MAX_HEADERS`) and 256 `Content-Type` parameters (`MIME_MAX_PARAMS`), and each count is charged as the entity is scanned rather than after it has been taken apart. A 1.4 MiB body declaring 200,000 empty parts previously split into all 200,000, and a 16 MiB header area took 1114 ms and 653 MiB of resident memory to read. A folded field spends one of the 1024 lines per physical line it occupies. `pki.est.splitMultipartMixed` and `pki.est.parseServerKeygenResponse` are held to the same part and header-line bounds, and raise `est/bad-multipart`. From `pki.smime.verify`, an entity over the part bound raises `smime/bad-multipart` and one over the header-line or parameter bound raises `smime/bad-mime`. The 16 MiB entity cap is unchanged and is still applied before any of the bytes are copied.

The record `pki.smime.verify` returns, and its `content`, no longer share the buffer the caller passed in. The parsed entity, its header area and its body were views into the caller's own bytes, so a write into that buffer after the verdict returned changed what the caller read back as verified. The entity is copied before it is read, the copy is byte-for-byte the input, and the octets a signature covers are unchanged.

The reference at [pkijs.com](https://pkijs.com) reads on a phone. At a 375px viewport the page scrolled 771px wide, and the nineteen navigation groups stood 659px tall even collapsed, so the first screen held navigation and no documentation. The content now starts under a compact header carrying the brand and a menu button, the navigation opens from that button, and tables and code blocks scroll inside their own box instead of widening the page. The menu is a label and a checkbox, so it works with JavaScript off, as the search form does. The layout at 721px and above is unchanged.
